text:
Key Takeaways:

Design Quality: Codex emerged as the winner in most subjective design rounds (0:28-15:16), often producing cleaner, more user-friendly interfaces with better visual storytelling compared to Claude Code, which frequently struggled with wordiness and layout bugs.

Efficiency: Codex consistently outperformed Claude Code in resource management, requiring about one-third of the time and only one-fifth of the output tokens per project (3:16-3:40).

Cost: Across the eight builds, Claude Code utilized 25 total agents and cost approximately $444 in estimated API fees, while Codex used 9 agents and cost roughly $100 (19:49-20:23).

The Impact of Prompting: During the final tests (18:00-19:28), the creator demonstrated that when prompts are highly detailed and specific, both models can produce nearly identical results, suggesting that specific instructions can bridge the gap between different AI harnesses.

In conclusion, while the creator uses both tools daily, they note that Codex is currently proving to be a more efficient and cost-effective option for these specific design tasks.
